title: NRC report RR-209 — egress-time estimates for single-family houses
jurisdiction: Canada (NRC research report; no project jurisdiction or AHJ identified)
code_edition: not assessed; the report reviews egress-time research and is not a code analysis

facts.text: The report says its estimates use literature review and prior studies; it notes that house egress time depends on fire location, occupant characteristics, alarms, building design and actions that delay egress.
A report table gives best-case and worst-case RSET estimates of 120 s and 970 s, composed of separate detection, alarm, pre-movement and travel assumptions.

The report describes 25 subjects asked about evacuation from their own homes; it reports a mean travel distance of 16.6 m and mean evacuation time of 47 s, with 30–60 s used as travel-time estimates after the decision to evacuate.

limitations: This is a literature review and estimation report, not a full-scale building evacuation test or application.
